justifications.c1: Per-tree replacement costs of ~£450–£1,700 (Brighton & Hove, Haringey, Greenwich, RBWM; APSE figure unconfirmed in search) and scheme losses abroad ($20k Cornwall ON, $50k Falmouth ME); with £100+ probe hardware plus subscription, loss per tree is below 5× TCO.
justifications.c2: Watering rounds recur weekly to fortnightly in summer (Richmond 19 visits/yr search-confirmed, though its planting lists state a 10-visit baseline; Kingston 10/yr; Woodland Trust weekly) and mortality is high (Gloucester 95%, search-confirmed; USDA 19%/yr), but the pain is seasonal.
justifications.c3: Paid watering contracts are quantified: Windsor ON $4.37/tree/visit, Cockburn WA $658,793/yr, Richmond 19 visits/yr; the sensor would target rather than remove visits and no UK per-visit rate was found.
justifications.c4: LATF claims need a 75% survival survey and UTCF ties establishment payments to claims and a 5-year maintenance duty, but neither requires watering or moisture records; no statutory or insurer driver and no evidence of refused claims.
justifications.c5: Arboricultural officer adverts are evidenced but budget ownership is inconsistent (Huntingdonshire 'No budget', others manage contracts), councils are budget-constrained and sales go through public procurement.
justifications.c6: Grounds and tree contractors (Glendale, Kingston contracts) visit every tree, but there is no evidence they sell or bundle monitoring.
justifications.c7: Priced or piloted incumbents exist (Sensoterra $1,495, Climavi €1,274, Jena and Vienna city networks, Slough and Wrexham pilots), and these high prices plus no UK contractor-verification product suggest a gap, though it is inferred.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN soil probes exist (Dragino LSE01 £107.60, Milesight EM500-SMTC) with 3-year battery life evidenced, but the BOM is above £50 and vandalism or probe placement risk is unsourced.
justifications.c9: Value lasts only the 3-year establishment period per cohort and probes can be redeployed; no comparable subscription price was found.
justifications.c10: National and local news (ITV search-confirmed, GB News, Gazette, KPTV), first-hand complaints (FixMyStreet, Arbtalk), Westminster Hall debate and USDA study; no enforcement or insurer data.

weakest: The value per tree (about £450–£1,700 to replace, ~£150/yr grant) is too low to fund a £100+ probe plus subscription, and revenue ends after a 3-year establishment period.
